name: Kirchbichl
kurzbeschreibung: Historic Lower Inn Valley community with a celebrated natural peat lido, historic river barge yards, and cement heritage.
beschreibung:
Overview

Kirchbichl lies at an altitude of 515 metres in the Lower Inn Valley within the district of Kufstein. Home to around 5,980 residents, the municipality is picturesquely situated where the Brixentaler Ache flows into the Inn River, framed by the foothills of Mount Pendling and the nearby pilgrimage sanctuary of Mariastein. Kirchbichl is renowned across western Austria for its historic Moorstrandbad, one of Tyrol's oldest and warmest open-air lidos, fed by healing natural peat water. Serving as the strategic threshold between the Inn Valley and the Brixental, Kirchbichl weaves together a pioneering industrial past, idyllic river meadows, excellent transport connections, and versatile recreation for families and holidaymakers.

History

Human settlement on this sheltered hill traces back to prehistoric times: Mount Grattenbergl hosted a fortified settlement during the Hallstatt period. The town was first documented in 1152 as 'chirchpichl', referencing the church perched upon the knoll. For centuries, the riverside quarter of Kastengstatt served as a thriving shipyard and river landing for barges hauling precious salt, timber, and Schwaz silver down the Inn. In 1809, during the Tyrolean Rebellion, Grattenbergl became the fierce battleground where resistance leader Josef Speckbacher clashed with Bavarian and French armies. In 1858, industrialist Alois Kraft established the Austrian Empire's very first Portland cement manufactory in Kirchbichl, later known as Perlmooser Cement. The Baroque Parish Church of the Assumption of Mary was completed in 1733 by Jakob Singer, featuring dazzling Rococo ceiling frescoes by Matthäus Günther.

Getting There

Transport access to Kirchbichl is exceptional. Motorists reach the town directly via the Inntal Autobahn A12 at the Wörgl-Ost/Kirchbichl junction or via the B171 Federal Highway traversing the Lower Inn Valley. Rail travellers enjoy direct service at Kirchbichl railway station on the Lower Inn rail line, connected by S-Bahn line S8. Furthermore, the major railway junction of Wörgl Central Station lies only minutes away, offering seamless EuroCity, ICE, and Railjet links throughout Austria and Germany. The trans-alpine Inn Cycle Path R1 runs directly beside the town limits.

Tips

An essential summer highlight is the historic Moorstrandbad Kirchbichl. Built in 1933/34, this lakeside lido offers warm, mineral-rich peat water, spacious sunbathing lawns, and waterslides. History buffs can hike up the forested Grattenbergl hill, where commemorative markers explain the 1809 battle and a scenic lookout provides sweeping vistas across the Inn Valley. Cyclists can pedal along the scenic Inn Cycle Path or follow the popular Kaiser Bike Circuit. Just a short hop away stands the castle sanctuary of Mariastein, featuring its iconic forty-metre tower chapel, easily accessible on foot via a tranquil pilgrim path.
